parts.name: AMD / ASRock BC-250 specialty compute board, 16GB unified GDDR6
parts.igpu: GFX1013; stock boards commonly expose 24 CUs; community unlock work exists
parts.storage: M.2 NVMe; community reports describe limited PCIe link width
parts.expandability: non-standard mining/server board; no RAM upgrade
parts.power_range_w: roughly 55W community inference target at conservative clocks; higher unlocked configurations can draw far more
parts.plain_language: The BC-250 is the weird bargain worth tracking. It combines CPU and GPU access to 16GB of very fast GDDR6, which can make it surprisingly attractive for Vulkan inference. The tradeoff is significant: firmware, cooling, power delivery, Linux setup and GPU support are community-driven rather than plug-and-play. Treat every benchmark as board/revision/software specific and never assume a 40-CU unlock is safe or functional on every unit.
parts.source_notes: August 2026 community sale reports place individual boards around US$130-190. Community documentation reports 6C/12T, 16GB unified GDDR6 and working llama.cpp Vulkan inference. No official AMD retail specification page was found; experimental claims must remain community-labelled.

parts.name: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit, 8GB
parts.igpu: NVIDIA Ampere GPU; up to 67 INT8 TOPS platform AI performance
parts.storage: microSD plus NVMe support on carrier
parts.plain_language: This is one of the cleanest efficiency references in the catalog. NVIDIA gives it a mature CUDA/TensorRT/JetPack stack, and the board can run in a 7-25W envelope. The catch is memory: 8GB makes it excellent for small LLMs, embeddings, vision and control-plane AI, but it is not a replacement for a 32-96GB x86 node when model capacity is the goal.
parts.source_notes: NVIDIA currently lists the developer kit at US$249 and documents up to 67 INT8 TOPS, 102 GB/s memory bandwidth and 7-25W configurable power.

parts.name: Orange Pi 5 Plus, RK3588, 32GB LPDDR4X
parts.expandability: GPIO, PCIe/NVMe, eMMC, Wi-Fi module support
parts.power_range_w: 5V/4A board input; measure real inference wall power
parts.plain_language: A 32GB RK3588 board is interesting because it puts much more RAM than most SBCs into a very small power envelope. It can be a useful lightweight inference or always-on worker, but software support is less uniform than x86 or Jetson. Vulkan/NPU acceleration must be benchmarked with the exact Linux image and runtime instead of assumed from the 6-TOPS marketing number.
parts.source_notes: Orange Pi documents the 32GB model, RK3588 CPU, Mali-G610, 6-TOPS NPU and dual 2.5GbE. Alibaba results currently show Orange Pi 5 Plus families from roughly US$144.50 upward; exact 32GB SKU pricing must be confirmed.

parts.name: Radxa ROCK 5 ITX+, RK3588, 32GB LPDDR5x
parts.network: dual 2.5GbE reported for ITX+; verify board revision
parts.expandability: Mini-ITX form factor, standard power/case options, storage expansion
parts.power_range_w: Radxa documents CPU power under 10W and very low idle for ROCK 5 ITX family; measure complete-system wall power
parts.plain_language: This is the SBC that most resembles a real cluster motherboard. It fits Mini-ITX infrastructure, can carry 32GB of fast LPDDR5-class memory and has much richer storage/network expansion than tiny hobby boards. It is not the fastest LLM node, but its low power and dense packaging make it interesting for many-node experiments.
parts.source_notes: ALLNET China lists the 32GB ITX+ reference at US$235 but currently shows it sold out. Radxa documentation describes the RK3588 platform and low-power design.

parts.name: MINISFORUM BD795M motherboard with Ryzen 9 7945HX
parts.igpu: basic integrated Radeon graphics; CPU throughput is the main attraction
parts.expandability: mATX, PCIe x16, standard cooling/power ecosystem
parts.power_range_w: high-performance mobile CPU; should be power-capped for efficiency experiments
parts.plain_language: This is not the lowest-watt node, but it belongs in the project because it shows how far laptop silicon can scale when placed on a standard motherboard. Sixteen Zen 4 cores plus replaceable DDR5 and a full PCIe slot make it a strong heavy-worker reference, especially if benchmarks find an efficient power cap well below maximum boost power.
parts.source_notes: MINISFORUM currently lists the BD795M at US$367.90 with a soldered Ryzen 9 7945HX, 16 cores/32 threads and standard mATX-style expansion.

parts.name: Framework Laptop 13 Mainboard, Ryzen AI 5 340
parts.igpu: Radeon integrated graphics; NPU present on Ryzen AI platform
parts.expandability: designed for standalone use; documented modular ecosystem
parts.power_range_w: mobile platform; benchmark at constrained power targets
parts.plain_language: Framework mainboards are expensive compared with Alibaba barebones, but they are unusually clean standalone laptop motherboards: documented, modular and intended to be reused outside a laptop chassis. They make an excellent control/reference platform for comparing bargain boards against a maintainable commercial design.
parts.source_notes: Framework currently shows the Ryzen AI 5 340 Laptop 13 mainboard at a US$399 sale price.
